items.titleJa: 35日でフロントエンドの基礎を完全に理解する #26 - Nuxt①（ファイルベースルーティング・レイアウト・なぜNuxtか）
items.summaryJa:
Nuxtのファイルベースルーティングと SSR の仕組みを、本文の事実のみで要約します。

Nuxtを使う主な理由は2つある。1つは規約で決まっているため、ルーティングやレイアウト、フォルダ構成、ビルド設定などを毎回ゼロから設計せず済むこと。2つ目は、初期設定で SSR が付いてくることによって、サーバー側で HTML を組み立てて返せる点で、JavaScript を実行しない相手にも中身が届く点と、初回表示が速くなる効果があることです。

ファイルベースルーティングにより、app/pages/ にファイルを置くだけで、それがそのまま URL に対応します。例として index.vue を置けば /、about.vue を置けば /about となり、動的ルートは [id].vue のようにファイル名で表現できます。Nuxt では useRoute などの Vue Router の機能はそのまま使え、import は不要な自動インポートです。

レイアウト機能により、全ページ共通の枠を app/layouts/default.vue に記述し、<slot /> を介して各ページを差し込みます。これによりヘッダーやフッターを共通化しつつ、個別のページ本体だけを書く構成が可能です。SSR の仕組みは、curl のような JavaScript を実行しないリクエストでも、サーバーが HTML を事前組み立てして返す点に表れます。

nuxt.config.ts には設定を集約し、ルーティングやビルド設定などをここだけで管理します。実際に試す際は、Nuxt アプリを作成して app/app.vue を NuxtLayout/NuxtPage の形へ書き換え、4つのファイルを用意して動かします。

items.title: Introducing Geist Serif
items.summary: Geist started as a monospace typeface for developers, built for the editors and terminals where they spend their day doing their work. From there it grew into Geist Sans for product interfaces, and then into Geist Pixel, which was inspired by the grids of early computer screens. Today, we're adding a new member to the family: Geist Serif . Geist Serif is a high-contrast display serif built on the same foundations as Geist Sans, Geist Mono, and Geist Pixel. It has fine, saw-toothed serifs and sharp hairlines, and it was drawn to communicate messages powerfully both in the physical world and on the high-density screens on modern devices. Same system, new voice At Vercel, Geist Sans runs the product. For headlines, though, we wanted a second voice, one that belongs to the same system, instead of a stranger picked from a drop-down menu. A lot of tech brands have moved away from clean sans-serifs to get some personality back, and many of them borrow from vintage computer ads. Geist Serif takes a different path: toward fashion, editorial design, and magazine headlines. It's our homage to the artists behind Rolling Stone and Harper's Bazaar . From the beginning, each Geist family has read from a chapter of type history: the Swiss design movement, early terminal and DOS computing, and now editorial print. Display first Geist Serif began as a set of sketches by Evil Rabbit , which Andrés Briganti then expanded. The first letters already showed an expressive serif, in the spirit of typefaces like Victor Serif and Stanley. When Mark Davis took over the drawings, we made the first release a display face for headlines, posters, and other large sizes, while work on the full family continued. Print has always struggled to hold fine hairlines and sharp serifs, but today's displays can handle a high level of detail. We wanted the new face to take full advantage of modern screens, so we thinned every downstroke by 50% and tightened the sidebearings to push the contrast as far as it would go. Each serif has a wedge on one side and a curve on the other, so the proportions are classical and look beautiful in print, but the construction is new and optimized for digital devices. From the first prototype to today The first prototype of Geist Serif was shared on April 1, 2026. Here's the same word, Geist, in that prototype, compared with the display drawing shipping today. Geist grew teeth The goal was to honor our original intent and keep the serif closely tied to the sans, even when the letters sit on top of each other. Geist Serif’s stems match Geist Sans, and the two share widths and postures. The saw-toothed serifs and high contrast give Geist an editorial voice. One phrase kept coming up as each character was drawn: “Geist grew teeth.” Four families, one x-height Geist Serif uses the same cap height and x-height as Geist Sans, so you can drop it into any Geist layout without moving a line. Mix Sans, Mono, Pixel, and Serif in the same sentence and every word looks the same size. Metric Geist Sans Geist Serif UPM 1000 1000 Cap height 710 710 x-height 530 530 Ascender 710 750 Descender -150 -200 Four variants, one axis Like Geist Pixel, Geist Serif has a variable axis that swaps the shape of every dot in the font, including those on i and j and in punctuation. The axis is called Element Shape ( ELSH ), and it gives you four variants: Regular with round dots (the default), Square, Triangle (a nod to the Vercel logo), and Heart. Each variant also ships as its own static file. If you use the variable font, pick a variant with font-variation-settings : Crafted by hand In July the font had 227 glyphs . It now has 894 and covers 352 Latin-script languages, and we worked through more than 52,000 kerning pairs to get the spacing right. Some of the details are tiny. The eye of the g , for example, is tilted exactly 7°. Specs at a glance Geist Serif ships with: 1 weight (Regular) 4 variants (Regular, Square, Triangle, Heart) 894 glyphs 5 stylistic sets ( ss01 to ss05 ) 352 supported languages Getting started Geist Serif ships in the same package as the rest of the family: Exports and CSS variables: GeistSerif (variable, all shapes): --font-geist-serif GeistSerifRegular : --font-geist-serif-regular GeistSerifSquare : --font-geist-serif-square GeistSerifTriangle : --font-geist-serif-triangle GeistSerifHeart : --font-geist-serif-heart Each one has its own entry point, so you only ship the font file you use. For example, in layout.tsx with GeistSerifRegular : You can also download the font files, test every stylistic set, and inspect each glyph at vercel.com/font . What’s next Regular is the first style we’re releasing, and the rest of the family is already in progress. We’re testing future versions while building this one, so this release is just the start. Weights from Thin to Black The variable font will range from Thin (100) to Black (900). In this week’s proofs, the g in Black is the letter we can’t stop looking at. Toward a text face To explore a text version, we built a foundry tool that measures strokes, including where they meet, and thickens the display outlines. It edits the outlines directly, so we can set real words and see which strokes need more weight. Italics, built rule by rule We’re also developing an italic generated entirely in Python. We slanted existing italics back upright and compared them with their romans. With the angle removed, the remaining differences show up clearly, and we turned them into rules we can test and revise. This italic won’t be the final version, but breaking glyphs in code helps us find the limits faster. More scripts and Google Fonts Cyrillic support is planned to match Geist Sans and Geist Mono, and Geist Serif will come to Google Fonts after launch. One family With Geist Sans, Geist Mono, Geist Pixel, and now Geist Serif, the family runs from UI text and code to expressive display type, and all four feel at home together. Download Geist Serif and start building. Thank you to everyone who made Geist Serif possible. None of this would have been possible without an incredible group of people behind the scenes. Huge thanks to Andrés Briganti for starting this journey with me and drawing the first version that everything else grew from, and to Mark Davis for carrying it across the finish line with obsessive craft, from the expanded glyph set and variable axis to every last kerning pair. Thanks also to Patrick McDonald and Marijana Pavlinić for the poster designs, to Luis Gutierrez Rico for the motion and incredible magic, to Christopher Kindl for shipping the package and rebuilding the landing page down to the smallest details, and to Zahra Jabini for the coordination and technical support that brought it all together. This was a true team effort, and I’m grateful to have built it with all of you. Read more

items.title: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host
items.summary: The fx adapter for the AI SDK’s HarnessAgent now uses libfx , the TypeScript library for fx. The harness and model requests run in your application’s process, while built-in filesystem and shell operations remain isolated in the sandbox. This simplifies sandbox setup: you no longer need to install fx inside the sandbox, run a sandbox bridge, or expose a sandbox port. Model credentials stay on the host, outside the environment where the agent runs commands. The rewrite also adds: Built-in tool filtering: choose which built-in tools the agent can use Mid-turn steering: send new instructions while a turn is running Structured output: generate responses that match a schema Image tool results: return images to the model through toModelOutput() Sessions can be saved and resumed in a new host process. Update @ai-sdk/harness-fx to the latest version to use the new adapter. Learn more in the fx harness documentation . Read more

items.title: Introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway . Virtual Models are an abstraction of the model string and configurations your apps and developers use. With a single virtual model ID, you can change and update models, configure fallbacks and priority, and enforce Zero Data Retention centrally. The virtual model configuration applies wherever the ID is used. Assign a virtual model ID to an agent task, and pass it as the model string wherever that task is called. You can then change the model and settings behind the virtual model ID in AI Gateway, and your apps and agents will pick up the new configuration automatically, without code changes or redeploys. New models use the same virtual model ID In the last 90 days, 125 new models from more than 10 labs became available on AI Gateway. That adds up to about 10 a week. AI Gateway already makes switching a one-line change. You call any of those models by ID, and AI Gateway routes each request to a healthy provider and can fall back to others when one fails. That one line still lives in your code, so switching usually means a redeploy. Virtual Models move model selection and configuration to AI Gateway. You create an ID for a task, like vmc/coding-agent , and then configure the model and the settings it should use: You can then use that virtual model ID as the model string wherever the task runs: For coding agents like Claude Code , Codex , and others, connect them with vercel ai-gateway setup , then select your virtual model in each harness's model picker or configuration. When a different model is available, including one from another provider, edit the virtual model . Every app and agent that calls vmc/coding-agent picks it up within a few minutes, with no code change or deployment needed: Give each task its own model An agent task like support ticket triage can run hundreds of times an hour and needs to be cheap. Other tasks, like legal contract review, may only run a few times a day, but require a high level of reasoning. You can now give each task a purpose-built virtual model and easily evolve that model and configuration over time: Settings such as fallbacks, Zero Data Retention, and tags stay with the virtual model when you switch models. Provider options apply per provider, so an Anthropic-specific setting stops applying when you point the virtual model at an OpenAI model. Review your provider options whenever you switch providers. Before you switch a virtual model that serves production traffic, point a second one, like vmc/coding-agent-candidate , at the new model and run your evals against it. If quality drops after the switch, point the original back at the previous model. Govern which models your team uses and how Anyone on your team can call a virtual model, and team roles control who can make changes to it. Platform and security teams can centrally govern and test models and settings, while still easily giving teams access to new models as they are released. Settings on a virtual model win over the same settings in a request, so callers can't override the provider order, fallbacks, or service tier you chose. For example, you can configure the fallback models for vmc/storefront-assistant centrally, and every app using that virtual model ID will use the same failover configuration, even if a request specifies different fallbacks. If a virtual model requires Zero Data Retention or providers that don't train on request data, those configurations are enforced even if a request explicitly sets zeroDataRetention or disallowPromptTraining to false. Tags on a virtual model replace any tags sent with the request, so spend lands on the task no matter how each app tags its calls. The Virtual Models page shows requests, spend, and success rate for each task. Get started Create a virtual model from your team dashboard or with the Vercel CLI . About AI Gateway AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and doesn't charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Virtual Models work with every model type on AI Gateway, including image, video, speech, embedding, and realtime models, and with the AI SDK and the OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs. See the Virtual Models documentation for every setting. Read more

items.title: The spyware hiding in old script tags
items.summary: 🚀 Frontend Focus #​764 — October 28, 2026 | Read on the web 🖼️ HTML-in-Canvas: Interactive DOM Inside 2D, WebGL and WebGPU Canvases — Arriving in stable Chrome next week, this long-incubated API draws real, live HTML into 2D, WebGL and WebGPU canvases, with text selection, form controls, Find-in-Page and screen readers all still working. Three.js, Babylon.js and PixiJS already support it. Chrome-only for now, but a big leap for canvas-heavy UIs. There's a related video here too . Natalia Markoborodova (Chrome) Creating Dynamic Social Media Cards for User Content — Chris digs into how links unfurl across Discord, X, Slack, Bluesky, iMessage and more, and argues most dynamic social cards waste the image by just restating the title and description. Then he shows what should go on it instead. Chris Coyier Would You Let Your AI Agent Grade Its Own Homework? — Agents write code faster than ever. They even review their own work. But who’s reviewing them? Dropbox, Notion & ElevenLabs don’t take the risk. With Meticulous, every change is exhaustively verified, with zero developer effort. Meticulous sponsor DeadTag: Forgotten Third-Party Script Tags Became a Delivery Network for Spyware — Attackers are buying up expired domains once used by analytics, ad and widget scripts, so any site still carrying the old tag now silently loads attacker code. A worthy reminder to go audit those tags! Scott Helme ⚡️ IN BRIEF 🎉 CSS-Tricks , after a spell under the ownership of DigitalOcean, is independent once again under the stewardship of editor Geoff Graham . 🦊 Firefox 159 enables scroll-driven animations by default, so they now work in all major engines. It also adds scoped custom element registries. 🪪 Since Chrome 155, sites can use the Digital Credentials API to offer credentials , such as digital IDs, to a compatible wallet app on the user's phone. ⚙️ W3C has launched a polyfill pilot for WebMCP , a JavaScript API that exposes web app functionality as agent-callable tools. 🌅 The Arc browser is being sunset this December, and Dia is suggested as a viable alternative. Zen is another, non-Chromium variant. 📺 Firefox has ▶️ a new ad with various 'meme icons' from years gone by (Numa Numa Guy kicks things off). 📙 Articles, Opinions & Tutorials WebKit Features for Safari 27.1 — A fresh release of Safari came out alongside Apple's new foldable. There's advice on how to create layouts for folding screens using Device Posture API and the Viewport Segments API . Both are behind feature flags for now. Jen Simmons (WebKit) 💡 Safari 27.2 followed days later , adding ::field-content for styling a customizable select's displayed text, and renaming Grid Lanes' flow-tolerance to fit-tolerance . Investigating a Curious Case of Font Format Fallbacks — Paul chases a bug in which a site's font loaded three times in a row , as WOFF2, then WOFF, then TTF, following the browser's error messages into Chromium's own source to find the cause. Paul Calvano 🗓️ Workshop: How to Implement Session Replay — Filters, custom tags, and sampling settings for finding the sessions that matter. Nov 5, 10am PT. Sentry sponsor Performance Budgets Need a Representative Worst — Harry revises his own long-standing advice: a budget set from your single worst result lets one outlier hide real regressions, so start from a representative worst (P90 or P95 of recent data) instead. A spreadsheet template is included. Harry Roberts ▶ The Most Vulnerable Week in Internet History — A fast recap of a rough security week: PHP2Shell (a pair of PHP engine bugs allowing unauthenticated RCE), a backdoored LiteLLM release, a CA with private keys that were numbers under 256, and more. Fireship Building an Isolated Preview for AI-Generated HTML — Any app that lets a model generate UI has to render the HTML it hands back. Keshav builds five demos showing how a preview can be attacked, then hardens it with iframe sandboxing, CSP and a carefully checked postMessage handler. Keshav Malik 🖨️ Websites Should Be Printable — Brennen printed his own site, didn't like the result, and walks through the print stylesheet changes that fixed it: a hidden header, 12pt type, and black links. Brennen Puth ▶ Why I'm Still Making CSS Tutorials — On caring about the craft of little details and why they matter in an age of agentic code generation. Kevin Powell 🧰 Tools, Code & Resources TitleArt: Make Text Like It's 1997 — Aww yeah, a big dose of nostalgia for users of Microsoft Office back in the 90s. Every classic WordArt style, shape and 3-D effect recreated in the browser. Davey Barker The “Last 90 Days” Filter Shouldn’t Need a Spinner — Bigger date ranges mean your chart’s query scans more rows. TimescaleDB keeps it fast in Postgres. Get $1000 credit . Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor The Website Specification: Every Technical Detail a Site Needs Before Launch — A checklist you (or an agent) can work through before launch, covering SEO, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, i18n, and more. Joost de Valk browser-whisper 2.0: In-Browser Audio and Video Transcription with WebGPU — A library that runs Whisper, Moonshine and other speech models entirely in the browser over WebGPU (with a WASM fallback), complete with timestamped segments, cached models and live mic input. Tanpreet Singh Jolly 🔊 UI SFX: A Library of 930+ Interface Sound Effects — 78 UI sound cues (clicks, toggles, success, add-to-cart, loading loops…) in 12 swappable styles, from minimal to arcade. A ~12KB runtime synthesizes them with Web Audio, or use the 936 CC0 MP3/Ogg files. Source code . Romain Simon MicroKit: 54 Copy-Paste React Microinteractions, CSS-First — Free animated buttons, hover effects, tabs and inputs, each available in TS or JS and in plain CSS or Tailwind. About half need no dependencies, and they're the sort of little details that lift a UI. Henrique Barone 📰 Classifieds 📮 CraftForms : Hosted forms for any site, no backend needed. Two-line embed, unlimited submissions even on the free plan , no captcha. 🧾 Add PDF editing to your app with Foxit's API : Merge, split, rotate, replace pages and flatten annotations, with working code. 🌿 ...and finally Overgrown: When Plants Invade Your Abandoned Tabs — Leave a tab unread too long and this Chrome extension has vines grow across it, until you work your way back in with a machete, chainsaw or flamethrower(!). It's not on the Web Store, so load it unpacked from the repo . Charlie Gerard

items.title: Run Paseo agents on Vercel Sandbox
items.summary: Paseo now supports running fx, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi in the cloud with the Vercel Sandbox plugin . You can now start an agent in Vercel Sandbox from Paseo on your laptop, then connect from your phone to control the same session, even when your laptop is closed. Stopping a sandbox saves your files and conversation history so you can pick up where you left off. Active processes stop with the sandbox. Enter your Vercel AI Gateway key once during setup. The plugin reuses it for model requests across your sessions, keeping the key outside the sandbox. To get started, enable plugins in Settings → Plugins in Paseo. Then install the plugin: Learn more in the Sandbox documentation , Paseo plugin listing , and the Paseo related projects documentation . Read more

items.title: Particle-1 is now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Particle-1 from Particle AI is now available on AI Gateway . It is post-trained on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, with a focus on completing software engineering tasks using fewer tokens. Particle describes the gains as shorter reasoning, fewer rounds of trial and repair, and more focused exploration. Use it for debugging, planning code changes, and breaking down multi-step engineering problems. Particle-1 has a 1M-token context window for working with code and extended task histories. Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in your environment. Use particle/particle-1 as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest version of Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select particle/particle-1 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Particle-1 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

items.summaryJa: Anthropicは医薬品開発の加速を目的に、Sixつの組織と共同研究を進めつつ自社の薬物探索にも着手。 Claudeを用いて設計->製造->規制提出までの多様なタスクを統合的に支援する取り組みを進め、各社のケーススタディと技術報告を公表している。 具体例として、Generate BiomedicinesはCAR-T細胞療法の設計短縮と性能向上、Divergence LabsはIgE除去を狙う二腕設計の探索、BigHat Biosciencesはリードの結合・安定性・凝集性を改善、Envedaは製造記録と規制文書の自動化・初稿作成、TCGはClaudeを用いた新会社設立による創薬プログラムの拡大を挙げている。
